newsitem.title: USA: KCP&L says majority don't want Western bid.
newsitem.headline: KCP&L says majority don't want Western bid.

text.p: Kansas City Power & Light Co said on Monday that the majority of its shareholders do not support a merger with Western Resources.

"All anyone has to do is look at the number of shares tendered to Western to see that a clear majority of KCPL shareholders have not supported a Western/KCPL combination," KCPL chairman Drue Jennings said in a statement.
Western said on Sunday that more than 44 percent of KCPL shares have been tendered and that it has extended its offer deadline to November 15.
In a newspaper advertisement on Monday, Western Resources said that by tendering more than 27.1 million shares so far, "KCPL shareowners are calling on the board to make this a friendly merger now."
Lack of shareholder support forced Kansas City Power to abandon its friendly merger agreement with UtilitCorp United Inc after a rival tender offer by Western Resources emerged.
"Our board has rejected Western's hostile exchange offer, and continues to recommend that shareholders not tender their shares to Western," Jennings said in the statement.
